title: Focus a diode laser before cutting robot parts: lower its free-sliding module onto the focus bar, lock it, stow the bar
instruction: Focus the laser module on this plywood sheet before the robot-arm parts are cut. Flip the focus bar down. Hold the module so it cannot drop, loosen the thumb-screw handle, and lower the module until the bar just rests on the sheet. Tighten the handle, flip the bar back up onto its magnet, and let go of everything. Do not move the sheet.
context: Robot builders cut plate parts from 3 mm sheet on desktop laser cutters; the MeArm robot arm's parts fit on 300 x 200 mm of 3 mm sheet. An open-frame diode laser such as the xTool D1 Pro has no autofocus, so before each cut its module is set by hand. The D1 Pro Quick Start Guide: "Put the focal length setting bar down", "Loosen the thumb screw on the other side and slide the laser module upward or downward", "After determining the position, tighten the thumb screw and put the focal length setting bar back"; and "Prevent the middle plate and laser module from falling down themselves." Loosened, the module runs freely down its slide, so one hand carries it 12 mm down onto the bar's contact while the other works the handle. It must not drop, and must stay within 0.5 mm of that contact as the handle locks: a 3 mm through-cut has to sit inside the module's 4 mm depth of focus. A robot that does this can run the machine that cuts its own parts.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (61 cm apart at the table's near edge), x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Nothing is random. Laser: an xTool D1 Pro 20W open-frame diode laser engraver (455 nm), unplugged: red anodised aluminium frame 59 x 60 cm, rails 4 cm wide and 5 cm tall, square on the table at x 19 to 78, y -30 to +30; gold aluminium gantry beam 4 x 4 cm along y, 11 to 15 cm up, front face at x 35.5, pushed back by hand so the laser module's axis is at (29, 6); its carriage plate stands behind the module. Honeycomb: xTool's honeycomb working panel, 50 x 50 x 2.2 cm, aluminium honeycomb on an aluminium base, at x 24.5 to 74.5, y -25 to +25. Sheet: 3 mm basswood plywood, 30 x 20 cm, 80 g (estimate), loose on the honeycomb, long side along y, at x 25 to 45, y -10 to +20; tape marks on the honeycomb at its two front corners. Laser module (the D1 Pro's 20 W module, 0.8 kg, estimate): red anodised aluminium body 6 x 6 cm, 12.8 cm from the orange acrylic light shield's lower edge to the fan housing's top; it slides vertically on its carriage. Thumb-screw handle on its -y side: a black lever 3 cm long on a steel screw 2 cm out from the face, 6 cm above the shield edge, pointing at the robot when tight. Focal length setting bar on its +y side: a steel strip 8 x 3 mm with a rounded end, 4.8 cm from pivot to tip, on a bracket 1 cm off the face, pivoting 1.5 cm behind the front face and 4 cm above the shield edge; hanging, its tip is 8 mm below the shield edge. Start: the module locked with its shield edge 4.5 cm up, so the hanging bar's tip would be 12 mm above the sheet; the bar stowed on its magnet, 10 degrees short of upright, leaning toward the robot. Both grippers open at the ready pose.
scoring: Real-trial tools: overhead and wrist video; a phone filming 240 fps slow motion on a small tripod 40 cm to the robot's left of the module, level with it and aimed at its +y face, with a 150 mm steel rule taped upright to the carriage plate beside that face and a pen line across the face; a taper gap gauge (1 to 15 mm); a digital caliper; a 0.5 mm feeler blade; a luggage scale; a ruler; tape marks. Focus error e: the hanging bar's tip height above the sheet; real: the gap under the light shield's front lower edge (taper gauge) minus the hanging bar's reach below that edge (caliper); sim: the slide's position against the bar's contact position. In focus: e within 0.5 mm. Near focus: e within 2.0 mm. Locked: real, a 10 N downward pull on the module (luggage scale on a cord loop) moves it under 0.2 mm (the taper-gauge gap under the shield, read before and after the pull); sim, the handle within 10 degrees of its tight stop. Bar stowed: on its magnet, within 10 degrees of its stowed angle. Released and still: both grippers (fingers and palm) 3 cm or more from the module (with its bar and handle) and from the sheet; the module, bar, handle and sheet each under 1 cm/s (sim: under 0.5 mm of movement in each 50 ms step). Latched 0 at any moment: (1) dropped: the module descends faster than 3 cm/s at any moment, touched or not (more than 1.5 mm within any 50 ms), or descends 2 mm or more while no gripper touches its body (its bar and handle do not count), from its highest point since a gripper last touched it (real: the pen line against the rule on the 240 fps video, frame by frame; sim: the slide's descent over each 50 ms control step, and finger contacts every 240 Hz physics step); (2) moved: any sheet corner, or the module along either axis, more than 3 mm from its tape mark. A held module lowered faster than 3 cm/s counts as dropped too: the xTool D1 Pro Quick Start Guide warns "Prevent the middle plate and laser module from falling down themselves. Otherwise, the limit pieces may be damaged." A steady, held lowering stays well under 3 cm/s; a module falling freely passes it within 0.1 mm. Otherwise, at the end of the trial: 1.0: in focus, locked, bar stowed, released and still, held 1 s. 0.75: in focus, locked, released and still; bar not stowed, or the 1.0 state held under 1 s. 0.5: near focus but not in focus, locked, released and still. 0.25: in focus but unlocked (the module resting on its hanging bar), released and still. 0: anything else, or any latch.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Hold the module, loosen the handle, and lower the module until the hanging bar rests on a 12 mm drill bit's shank lying on the sheet; tighten the handle with its lever pointing at the robot, take the shank away and stow the bar. Put the sheet back on its tape marks, and the gantry so the module's tape marks line up. The machine stays unplugged throughout and the laser never fires; the module's cable stays connected, routed over the gantry as delivered. Cost: the D1 Pro 20W kit is about US$1,300 new; the laser never fires, so a used unit, even one with a failed laser, serves. xTool also sells the 20 W module on its own (retail model MD1PRO-L20) with its thumb screw, light shield and focal length setting bar; it sold for US$359.99 at a Woot clearance in October 2023 (no current price found) and fits a D1 Pro carriage's slot, held by its thumb screw. About 2 minutes per reset.
fidelity: Rigid bodies; frame, gantry and carriage fixed. Slide: a prismatic joint, 5 N s/m damping (estimate). Thumb screw: a lever hinge with no thread; lock rule in task.py holds the slide with a stiff drive carrying the module's weight while the lever is within 10 deg of its stop, so one swing frees or locks it (a real one may need re-indexing); handle rule gives 0.05 N m friction (estimate). Magnet rule holds the bar with 0.02 N m (estimate). focus_usd.py gives the 3 mm bar a 7 mm collider.
